new_entities.name: Azure Boards
new_entities.quote: Azure boards for planning, Azure repos for code

quotes.text: It's one connected platform that handles the entire software development lifecycle, planning, coding, testing, deploying, all in one place.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Compact definition of what Azure DevOps is.

quotes.text: Because manual deployments are the number one source of production incidents. Someone forgets the step. Someone copies the wrong file. Someone deploys to the wrong environment. Pipelines eliminate all of that.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: If something breaks, you know immediately. Not two weeks later when someone tries to deploy right away. The developer gets notified, they fix it, and they push again. Bugs get caught early when they're cheap to fix, not late when they're expensive.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the core value of continuous integration in plain language.

quotes.text: Those bugs are always the ones that could have been caught with a simple test. This is cheap insurance. It takes a little time up front, but it saves you a lot of pain later.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Persuasive case for structured testing that beginners often skip.

quotes.text: You don't need to adopt all five services at once. Pick one. Start with boards, create a project, track a few tasks, and see how it feels.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical, low-barrier recommendation for getting started.

chapters.title: Azure Repos: version control with Git
How it all fits together and first steps

takeaways: Azure DevOps is one connected platform of five services: Boards for planning, Repos for code, Pipelines for automation, Test Plans for quality and Artifacts for packages.
Linking work items, commits, pipeline runs, test cases and bugs gives full traceability from a user story to the deployed feature.
Start small on the free tier: create a project in Boards, track a few tasks, then add Repos and Pipelines one step at a time.
hook: Juggling separate tools for tasks, code, testing and deployment that never talk to each other? This episode explains Azure DevOps in plain English for beginners, makers and IT pros, and shows how its five connected services take a feature from idea to production.
